MAR.note: No exchange between the civil registry and the ID system is stated.
The civil registry is said to cover 100% of newborns but is not stated to be digital.
No data protection law is stated.
Transfer programmes are named but no payment channel is stated.

facts.fact: The ID4Africa slide gives 31 million citizens holding the electronic national identity card against a total Moroccan population of 36.6 million, about 85%.

MAR.note: No number given at birth is stated.
The slide labels a MOSIP use case but does not state who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.
No register keyed on the ID number is stated.

facts.fact: The ID4Africa slide lists the electronic national identity card as a key identification system in Morocco since 1977, held by 31 million citizens.

MAR.note: No system checking people against the ID is stated.

facts.fact: The ID4Africa slide lists the National Registry of Population (RNP) as in place since 2022, with 22 million citizens and resident foreigners of all ages.

MAR.note: No digital entry of births or deaths at local civil registration offices is stated.

facts.fact: The ID4Africa slide lists health insurance for vulnerable groups, direct cash transfer, higher education scholarship and health insurance for non-covered groups as achievements under the RNP-RSU system.

MAR.note: RNP-RSU is a targeting registry; no programme management information system is stated.

facts.fact: The ID4Africa slide dates the National System for Identifying and Targeting Beneficiaries of Social Programs (RNP-RSU) to December 2022 as a reform achievement.

The ID4Africa slide lists health insurance for vulnerable groups (11 million beneficiaries), direct cash transfer (3.9 million households), the Minhaty scholarship and health insurance for non-covered groups as achievements under RNP-RSU.
